sentences.en: So not only has everyone in England been pronouncing the name of her tribe wrong, she's also not even a queen.
sentences.zh: 所以不仅英国每个人都把她部落的名字读错了，她甚至都不是女王。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: So not in her own right, like Cotamundurus.
sentences.zh: 所以她不是凭自己的权利当女王，不像科塔蒙杜鲁斯。

sentences.en: So she's the consort of, well, the Romans call him a king, a rex, whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以她是配偶……好吧，罗马人称他为国王，一个雷克斯，随便什么都行。

sentences.en: I mean, he's the kind of the head honcho of the Icneianian.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是爱西尼人的领头羊。

sentences.en: A man called Prasutagas.
sentences.zh: 一个叫普拉苏塔格斯的男人。

sentences.en: So it's possible that Boudicca is, you know, she's come from another tribe.
sentences.zh: 所以布狄卡有可能……你知道，她来自另一个部落。

sentences.en: And the Icneian are a very distinctive people.
sentences.zh: 爱西尼人是一个非常独特的民族。

sentences.en: So it's telling that we haven't really talked about them to this point because they haven't really intruded on the narrative.
sentences.zh: 所以很说明问题的是，我们到目前为止还没有真正谈论过他们，因为他们还没有真正介入叙事。

sentences.en: They're not really a unitary kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是一个真正的单一王国。

sentences.en: They're a kind of a confederation, a kind of tribal league, pretty cohesive, but with separate subdivisions, kind of separate cantons, if you want to call them that.
sentences.zh: 他们是一种联盟，一种部落同盟，相当有凝聚力，但有各自的细分，有点像独立的行政区，如果你愿意这么叫的话。

sentences.en: They have had contacts with Rome pretty early on.
sentences.zh: 他们很早就与罗马人有过接触。

sentences.en: It's probable that they are one of the tribes that sent ambassadors to submit to Julius Caesar when he invaded back in 54.
sentences.zh: 很可能他们就是公元前54年尤利乌斯·恺撒入侵时派遣使者臣服的部落之一。

sentences.en: But it is striking, based on the archaeology, that the Icneian are much, much less in hock to Roman culture than the other major tribal groupings.
sentences.zh: 但根据考古发现，令人震惊的是，爱西尼人对罗马文化的接受程度远远低于其他主要部落群体。

sentences.en: And so, you know, you find there are very few Roman coins there, very little evidence of kind of luxury foreign goods, no amphora of wine, so on, things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你会发现在那里极少有罗马硬币，几乎没有外来奢侈品的证据，没有葡萄酒双耳瓶等等诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And so the question is, why should this be?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，为什么会这样呢？

sentences.en: And one answer might be their geographical circumstances.
sentences.zh: 其中一个答案可能与他们的地理环境有关。

sentences.en: You know, they're further north.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们处于更靠北的位置。

sentences.en: They're surrounded for much of their territory by the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 他们的领地大部分都被北海所包围。

sentences.en: And also the Fens, which at this time are very, very impassable for large stretches.
sentences.zh: 还有芬兰沼泽区，在当时，这一大片区域极其难以通行。

sentences.en: You know, they haven't been drained.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些地方还没有被排干。

sentences.en: So there's huge kind of swamps bordering the southern reaches of their territory.
sentences.zh: 所以在他们领地的南部边缘，环绕着巨大而泥泞的沼泽。

sentences.en: And you can kind of tell the way in which they're distinctive by looking at their coins, which we talked about in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 通过观察他们的硬币，你就能看出他们那种独特的方式，我们在上一集中也讨论过。

sentences.en: These are markers of a kind of cultural distinctiveness for the first time.
sentences.zh: 这些第一次成为了某种文化独特性的标志。

sentences.en: You can work out maybe what the ideology is of a particular tribal grouping by looking at them.
sentences.zh: 通过观察这些硬币，你或许能弄清楚某个特定部落群体的意识形态是什么。

sentences.en: And the thing that's striking about the Icneian coins, well, there's lots of stuff that's striking about them,
sentences.zh: 关于艾西尼硬币，最引人注目的是——当然有很多让人瞩目的地方——

sentences.en: but one of the really striking things is that unlike the coins of other British tribes, they feature very heavily the wolf, which by this point, it's quite rare in lowland Britain
sentences.zh: 但真正引人注目的事情之一是，与其他不列颠部落的硬币不同，它们的图案大量使用了狼。而在当时，狼在低地不列颠已经相当罕见

sentences.en: by this point.
sentences.zh: 在当时。

sentences.en: The wolf is very, very sinister.
sentences.zh: 这种狼非常非常阴森。

sentences.en: I've got one of their coins with a wolf on.
sentences.zh: 我有一枚他们铸造的刻有狼图案的硬币。

sentences.en: There's a brilliant description of it by Duncan McKay in his wonderful book, Echo Lens, which is a superb book about Boudicca, came out last year.
sentences.zh: 邓肯·麦凯在他那本精彩绝伦的书《回音透镜》（Echo Lens）中对此有过极其精彩的描述。这是一本关于布狄卡的超级好书，去年刚出版。

sentences.en: And he writes about this wolf.
sentences.zh: 他在书中写到了这只狼。

sentences.en: It's an emaciated, beak-jawed, spike-eared and spindle-limbed creature that must have moved more like a spider than anything mammalian.
sentences.zh: 它是一个消瘦、鸟喙状下巴、尖耳朵、细长肢体的生物，它的移动方式肯定更像一只蜘蛛而不是任何哺乳动物。

sentences.en: So very sinister.
sentences.zh: 所以非常阴森。

sentences.en: And it's shown with birds that are clearly associated with the fens.
sentences.zh: 而且它身边的鸟类图案明显与沼泽地有关。

sentences.en: So lapwings, bitterns, so on.
sentences.zh: 比如凤头麦鸡、麻鳽等等。

sentences.en: And this gives the sense that the wolf is a fen dweller, which in Germanic would be Fenrir.
sentences.zh: 这就给人一种感觉，这只狼是沼泽的栖息者，用日耳曼语来说就是芬里尔。

sentences.en: Oh, I love that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: And Fenrir in Norse mythology, of course, is the great wolf that at the end of the world devours the sun.
sentences.zh: 当然，在北欧神话中，芬里尔就是那只在世界末日吞噬太阳的巨狼。

sentences.en: And there's another kind of echo or perhaps foreshadowing of Norse mythology that another series of early Iconean coins features this strange mask-like male head with a single eye.
sentences.zh: 还有另一种对北欧神话的回响或预示，另一系列早期的艾西尼硬币上出现了一个奇怪的、类似面具的、单眼的男性头像。

sentences.en: And there's an Oxford numismatist called Daphne Nash-Briggs, who's written a lot about the Iconean coins in a very, very stimulating way.
sentences.zh: 牛津大学有一位名叫达芙妮·纳什-布里格斯的钱币学家，她以非常非常富有启发性的方式写了大量关于艾西尼硬币的文章。

sentences.en: And she writes about this eye, that its lids are either closed or firmly sewn shut, which of course may remind listeners of Odin, the one-eyed god who rips his eye out.
sentences.zh: 她写到了这只眼睛，它的眼睑要么是闭着的，要么是紧紧缝上的，这当然可能会让听众想起奥丁，那个挖掉自己一只眼的独眼神。

sentences.en: Gave up his eye for wisdom.
sentences.zh: 为了智慧而放弃了自己的眼睛。

sentences.en: I mean, what's even more fascinating is that Nash-Briggs argues that Iconean coins, in addition to having Latin and Bretonic language, also has Germanic language.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，更让人着迷的是，纳什-布里格斯认为艾西尼硬币除了拉丁语和布立吞语之外，还包含日耳曼语。

sentences.en: When you say argues that, is that because it's up for debate?
sentences.zh: 当你说是“认为”时，是因为这还有待商榷吗？

sentences.en: You can't really tell what it says.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法确定上面写的是什么。

sentences.en: So it's massively up for debate.
sentences.zh: 所以这有着巨大的争议。

sentences.en: And I think that other scholars would say these seeming foreshadowings of Norse mythology, the details of Norse mythology come millennia later.
sentences.zh: 我想其他学者会说，这些对北欧神话貌似预示的东西，其北欧神话的细节是在几千年后才出现的。

sentences.en: It's most improbable that these stories were current at that time.
sentences.zh: 这些故事在当时就已经流传的说法是极不可能的。

sentences.en: The linguistic evidence is also furiously debated.
sentences.zh: 语言学证据也受到了激烈的争论。

sentences.en: But I mean, my gut feeling is that it's perfectly plausible that the Icone, because they
sentences.zh: 但我的直觉是，艾西尼人完全有可能是因为他们

sentences.en: are open to the North Sea in the way that, say, Wales or Cornwall had been open to Celtic influences coming up from the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 面向北海，就像比如说威尔士或康沃尔曾面向从大西洋北上的凯尔特人影响一样。

sentences.en: It seems to me perfectly plausible that there might be a kind of Germanic substratum in their culture.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，他们的文化中存在某种日耳曼语底层是完全有可能的。

sentences.en: And that perhaps these coins reflect traditions that are percolating around long, long before the Viking period.
sentences.zh: 也许这些硬币反映了早在维京时期之前很久就在各处流传的传统。

sentences.en: It's plausible that there are traders and things crossing the North Sea, isn't it, in this period?
sentences.zh: 在这一时期，有商贩之类的人穿梭于北海，这是很合乎情理的，对吧？

sentences.en: Maybe not at the same volume as centuries later, but there must have been sea contacts between East Anglia and Holland or Denmark or Norway or whatever.
sentences.zh: 也许其规模不像几个世纪后那么大，但东盎格利亚与荷兰、丹麦或挪威等地之间肯定存在海上联系。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems improbable that there wouldn't be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果没有这些联系，反倒显得不可能了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it perhaps offers a clue as to where Iconean culture is coming from, that perhaps this is why
sentences.zh: 这或许为艾西尼文化的来源提供了一条线索，也许这就是为什么

sentences.en: they are less influenced by what's happening in Gaul, but more influenced perhaps by Germanic traditions that are crossing from Saxony or from Scandinavia or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们受高卢发生的事情影响较小，而更多地受到来自萨克森、斯堪的纳维亚或其他地方的日耳曼传统的潜在影响。

sentences.en: And is it not the case that they are consciously more isolationist and more exceptionalist so that
sentences.zh: 而且，难道不是因为他们有意采取更加孤立主义和更加例外主义的态度，以便

sentences.en: they are deliberately restricting Roman imports and resisting the advance of Roman culture, again, this is an argument that Daphne Nash-Briggs pushes.
sentences.zh: 他们刻意限制罗马进口商品并抵制罗马文化的推进——这也是达芙妮·纳什-布里格斯所坚持的观点。

sentences.en: She points out that there must be Roman coins coming in because there's gold and silver that's being reminted, but it seems that they all
sentences.zh: 她指出，罗马硬币肯定有流入，因为有黄金和白银被重新铸造，但看起来它们似乎

sentences.en: seem to have been deliberately melted down and that there must almost certainly be conscious restrictions on the import of wine.
sentences.zh: 全都被蓄意熔化了，而且几乎可以肯定对葡萄酒的进口存在刻意的限制。

sentences.en: And she suggests that it was an attempt, quote, to mitigate destructive competition amongst armed aristocrats.
sentences.zh: 她认为这是一种尝试，引述：“为了减少武装贵族之间破坏性的竞争。”

sentences.en: And if that's the case, then it must be Prasutogas who is responsible for that.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，那么对此负责的一定是普拉苏托古斯。

sentences.en: And it suggests that he's walking a very delicate tightrope because the probability, and again, we're talking in terms of probability or
sentences.zh: 这表明他正走在一条非常微妙的走钢丝般的路上，因为可能性——同样，我们这里是在讨论可能性或

sentences.en: possibility here, is that he was a hostage in Rome.
sentences.zh: 机缘——是他曾在罗马当过人质。

sentences.en: The royal children of British tribes seem to have been sent to Rome as a matter of course.
sentences.zh: 不列颠部落的王室子女似乎作为惯例都被送往了罗马。

sentences.en: So he would be conscious of Roman power and Roman culture.
sentences.zh: 所以他对罗马的力量和罗马文化会有所了解。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he clearly seems to have had a role in Iconean life that was more than that of just a king.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他在艾西尼人生活中的角色显然不仅仅是一个国王那么简单。

sentences.en: He seems to have held a kind of priestly status.
sentences.zh: 他似乎拥有某种祭司的身份。

sentences.en: And it's likely that
sentences.zh: 并且很有可能

sentences.en: Prasutogas is not a proper name but a title because based on the evidence of his coins, it seems to have
sentences.zh: 普拉苏托古斯不是一个本名，而是一个头衔，因为根据他的硬币证据，它似乎

sentences.en: meant something like Pontifex Maximus, kind of high priest, the man who mediates between his people and the gods.
sentences.zh: 意味着类似于“最高祭司”的东西，一种大祭司，一个在其人民和神灵之间居中调停的人。

sentences.en: And I think it's telling in that context that Boudicca too, or more properly,
sentences.zh: 我认为在这种背景下很有说明意义的是，布狄卡也是如此，或者更确切地说，

sentences.en: Boudicca, I gather, this means she who brings victory, that this too may have been a title rather than a name.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，“布狄卡”这个名字的意思是“带来胜利的人”，这也可能是一个头衔而不是一个名字。

sentences.en: And it suggests that you have the victory giver marrying the man who is the mediator between the gods.
sentences.zh: 这就暗示了，胜利的赐予者嫁给了一个充当神灵调停人的人。

sentences.en: There is, Dominic, dare I say, a sacral dimension to this marriage.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我敢说，这场婚姻有着神圣的维系。

sentences.en: We love a sacral dimension on the rest of this history.
sentences.zh: 我们在这段历史的其余部分中非常热爱神圣的维度。

sentences.en: We so do.
sentences.zh: 我们确实如此。

sentences.en: And we can actually identify a place where this holy couple, because I think we should think of them as a kind of a holy couple, a sacral couple, where they may have presided.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上可以确定这对神圣夫妇——因为我认为我们应该把他们看作是一种神圣的夫妇，一对神圣的伴侣——可能曾经主持过仪式的地方。

sentences.en: Today, it's on an industrial estate called Fiss and Way.
sentences.zh: 如今，它坐落在一个叫做菲森韦（Fison Way）的工业园区里。

sentences.en: And Duncan McKay in his book has a brilliantly funny account of him trying to track down this place of eerie portent, you know, and this kind of crisp wrappers everywhere.
sentences.zh: 邓肯·麦凯在他的书中有过一段非常搞笑的记述，讲述了他试图寻找这个充满诡异预兆的地方，你知道的，到处都是那种薯片包装袋。

sentences.en: So when the industrial estate was being developed, archaeologists went in and they found that in the 50s AD, this massive artificial oak grove had been built there.
sentences.zh: 因此，当这个工业园区正在开发时，考古学家们进驻了，他们发现在公元50年代，这里曾建造过一个巨大的非自然橡树林。

sentences.en: So great serried ranks of posts and fences sticking up, deliberately trying to look like a grove of oaks.
sentences.zh: 那里有一排排巨大的柱子和栅栏耸立着，刻意营造得像一片橡树林一样。

sentences.en: So Nashbriggs says it's a symbolic grove.
sentences.zh: 所以纳什-布里格斯说这是一个象征性的树林。

sentences.en: You have, I mean, almost intangible, a sense of the Icani as a people for whom the dimension of the supernatural is everywhere and is part of their political dynamics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有一种几乎无法触及的感觉，即艾西尼人是一个超自然维度无处不在并将之作为其政治动力一部分的民族。

sentences.en: And I think that all of this helps to explain why the Icani, unlike the Catevoloni or the Trinovantes, are able to maintain their independence from Rome.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些都有助于解释为什么艾西尼人不像卡图沃劳尼人或特里诺范特人那样，能够保持他们对罗马的独立性。

sentences.en: Prasutogas is clearly a brilliantly competent politician.
sentences.zh: 普拉苏托古斯显然是一个极其精明的政治家。

sentences.en: He's able to reassure the Romans that his independence offers them no threat.
sentences.zh: 他能够让罗马人放心，他的独立对他们构不成任何威胁。

sentences.en: And at the same time, he's able to dampen down all the kind of ambitions among his fellow Iconeans, even to the extent that in 47, there's a kind of
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他能够压制同胞艾西尼人中间的所有野心，甚至在公元47年，当发生某种

sentences.en: Icanaean rebellion.
sentences.zh: 艾西尼人叛乱时也是如此。

sentences.en: But the Romans still don't, if they suppress it, possibly with the help of
sentences.zh: 但罗马人仍然没有——如果他们平息了这场叛乱，可能是在

sentences.en: Prasutogas, we don't know whether his collaboration went that far.
sentences.zh: 普拉苏托古斯的帮助下，我们不知道他的合作是否达到了那种程度。

sentences.en: But it is amazing that Prasutogas is able to maintain the independence of his people, even after an uprising like that.
sentences.zh: 但令人惊奇的是，即使在经历了这样一场起义之后，普拉苏托古斯仍然能够维护他的人民的独立。

sentences.en: But of course, the risk that face the Icani is that when Prasutogas dies, what will happen then?
sentences.zh: 但当然，艾西尼人面临的风险是，当普拉苏托古斯去世时，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: Tom, I have to tell you, I've just been looking at Feist and Wei.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不得不告诉你，我刚看了一下菲森韦。

sentences.en: It doesn't look very mystical at all.
sentences.zh: 它看起来一点也不神秘。

sentences.en: Not sacral.
sentences.zh: 一点也不神圣。

sentences.en: It looks like a brilliant place.
sentences.zh: 它看起来是个好地方。

sentences.en: If you're in Thetford and you need a new windscreen, I heartily recommend it.
sentences.zh: 如果你在塞特福德需要一块新挡风玻璃，我强烈推荐它。

sentences.en: That's the place.
sentences.zh: 就是那个地方。

sentences.en: But anyway, here he is in Feist and Wei near the windscreen place.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，他现在就在挡风玻璃修理厂附近的菲森韦。

sentences.en: And so the issue is that when he dies, late 59, early 60, what is going to happen to his kingdom that he has been able to preserve
sentences.zh: 所以问题在于，当他在59年末60年初去世时，他那在如此难以置信的动荡和冲突的政治环境中

sentences.en: in this incredibly turbulent and conflicted political environment?
sentences.zh: 得以保全的王国将会怎样？

sentences.en: Is he going to get the
sentences.zh: 他能把

sentences.en: Romans on board?
sentences.zh: 罗马人拉拢过来吗？

sentences.en: Is that part of his plan?
sentences.zh: 那是他计划的一部分吗？

sentences.en: That is his plan.
sentences.zh: 那确实是他的计划。

sentences.en: So Tacitus tells us what his plan is.
sentences.zh: 所以塔西陀告诉了我们他的计划是什么。

sentences.en: He writes,
sentences.zh: 他写道：

sentences.en: Prasutogas, king of the Icani, famed for his long prosperity, had made the emperor, so that's Nero
